title: British Dort judgment: daily lighter sins do not shake justification
source_text: XI. Hanc doctrinam aperte tradunt Theologi Magnae Britanniae, in suo judicio circa quintum Remonstrantium Articulum, quod insertum est actis Synodi Dordracenae. Ubi haec est eorum Thesis secunda: Electi, regenerati, & justificati, quamvis non peccare non possint, & leviora peccata subreptionis, negligentiae & inadvertentiae quotidie committant, eatenus tamen nec justificationis status concutitur, nec juris ad regnum coeleste haereditarii usus intercipitur.
pass_a_gloss: The theologians of Great Britain openly hand down this doctrine in their judgment concerning the fifth Remonstrant Article, which is inserted in the acts of the Synod of Dort. Where this is their second Thesis: The elect, regenerate, and justified, although they cannot but sin, and daily commit lighter sins of surprise, negligence, and inadvertence, yet so far neither is the state of justification shaken, nor is the use of the hereditary right to the heavenly kingdom intercepted.
pass_b_english: Britain’s Dort judgment: elect justified believers still sin lightly every day.
Those surprise and negligence faults do not shake justification or cut off heavenly inheritance.

choices.why: Justification status unshaken by lighter daily sins.
